key_insight: The paper simplifies and canonicalizes qudit measurement-based quantum computing flow, making adaptive correction analysis and flow finding more practical.
engineering_relevance: This gives a faster O(n^3) algorithm and reusable flow-preserving transformations for building, optimizing, and testing qudit-based quantum computation workflows.
method: Redefine qudit flow in a simpler form and show how to focus it canonically.
Improve the algebraic formulation to capture focused flow and support an O(n^3) flow-finding algorithm.
Study pivoting, vertex insertion/removal, and reversibility as flow-preserving transformations for optimization and generation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports algorithmic complexity improvements from O(n^4) to O(n^3) and states that the results are derived by extending known qubit flow theory to prime-dimensional qudits.
watch_item: The methods apply to prime-dimensional qudit graph states, so implementations must respect the dimensional and algebraic constraints of that setting.
paper_title: Working with measurement-based computations on qudits
